sections.html:
Margate is in Broward County. It was created as the Town of Margate on May 30, 1955 and took city status in 1961. The city covers about nine square miles with 30 miles of canals, sits 7.5 miles from the Atlantic and is roughly 20 minutes from Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport and Port Everglades. It provides its own police, fire and emergency medical services, water, wastewater and stormwater service, and it has 19 parks and recreational facilities.

  • Margate runs its own water and sewer, so request a final meter reading from the city at closing.
  • Canal frontage and distance to the coast are worth stating in a listing.
  • A buyer from outside Florida may ask about insurance, so gather your policy details.

sections.h2: Selling after a foreclosure suit starts
sections.html:
A Margate owner can still sell before the court sells the house for them. The lender files suit in Broward County and has to win a final judgment before the clerk sets any auction, which usually leaves more time than people expect.

After judgment the auction falls no later than 35 days and no sooner than 20 days out, unless the lender consents to a later date (s. 45.031). Notice runs for two consecutive weeks, the winning bidder posts a deposit, and 10 days of objection time follow the certificate of sale. Under s. 702.10 a lender can seek a faster order to show cause, but a granted homestead exemption on the latest roll creates a presumption of owner occupancy, which keeps a Margate homeowner on the ordinary track.

  • Read every court paper and note the response deadline printed on it.
  • Ask your servicer for a payoff figure in writing.
  • Call a Florida foreclosure attorney or legal aid office early.

Whatever remains after the lender and liens are paid is surplus, and the owner can claim it through the clerk. The judgment carries a notice about it, and homestead owners are told to check in within 10 days.

File your claim before the clerk reports the money as unclaimed. A voluntary sale on your terms usually leaves more control, because the closing agent pays off the mortgage and hands you the balance.

sections.h2: Early-payment discounts on Margate tax bills
sections.html:
Bills arrive in November, and unpaid taxes turn delinquent April 1. Paying early earns a sliding discount.

Early-payment discounts on a Broward tax bill
Month paidDiscount
November4 percent
December3 percent
January2 percent
February1 percent

Relief exists for owners who are short of cash. A homestead owner can defer part of the bill by filing Form DR-570 by March 31 following the assessment year. The deferral covers the amount above 5 percent of last year's household income, or above 3 percent when the permanent resident is 65 or older. Installment prepayment needs an application to the tax collector by May 1 (s. 197.222).

Skipped taxes lead to a certificate auctioned by June 1, with bidders competing to accept the lowest interest in quarter-percent steps (s. 197.432). The certificate holder is barred from pressing the owner for payment during the first two years, counted from April 1 of the year of issue.

After that, a tax deed application can be filed for a $75 fee (s. 197.502). The clerk runs the auction, and on homestead land the opening bid includes one-half of the latest assessed value. Before listing, ask the Broward tax collector whether any certificate is attached to the parcel.

sections.h2: What to gather before talking to a buyer
sections.html:
Round up the papers a buyer will ask about first so the offer matches the house's true condition. Missing paperwork is a frequent reason closings run late.

  • The mortgage statement with a current payoff figure.
  • Court papers, if a foreclosure suit has been filed, with the case deadlines marked.
  • Your newest tax bill, plus a note of any certificate on the parcel.
  • Any homestead exemption notice from the property appraiser.
  • Names of everyone on the deed, since all owners must sign.

Florida requires a land transfer to be written and signed in front of two witnesses, and witnessing may happen by audio-video technology (s. 689.01). Plan signing early when an owner lives out of state. For exemption questions, call the Broward County Property Appraiser at 954-357-6830.

sections.h2: Which offers suit an owner in a hurry?
sections.html:
A cash purchase makes sense when a court date, a tax certificate or a lien sets the pace. It removes financing and appraisal delay, and repairs become the buyer's job.

Get the closing date, the payoff and each fee on paper first. Ask whether the deposit can be refunded, who picks the title company, and how a request for more time would be handled. Comparing two or three written offers with the same lines filled in helps you spot the weak ones fast.

If you plan to stay a few weeks after closing, ask for a short rent-back in writing, with a daily rate and a move-out date. Take photos of the house at handover so both sides agree on its condition.

sections.h2: Services for older sellers and retiree buyers
sections.html:
The Northwest Focal Point Senior Center serves adults age 60 and older in the city and county, with transportation, an eldercare advocate, home energy assistance and meals. An older owner selling to move closer to family can ask the center what help is available before the move, and retiree buyers may ask about these services too.

The city also has a fire department rated ISO Class I and a Community Redevelopment Agency created in 1996. Keep your listing description plain and let a buyer confirm the details with the city.

sections.h2: From signed contract to funds in hand
sections.html:
After you sign, the title company runs a search for mortgages, liens and any tax certificate. You then review a settlement statement showing payoff, deed tax, recording and any prorated taxes. At signing the deed is witnessed, recorded with the clerk, and the balance is sent to you.

If your mortgage is in default, give the title company the lender's contact information and any court papers so the payoff can be confirmed. Sell before the auction date and you keep control of the price and the timing.

Start outside. Margate's canals and tree-lined streets make curb appeal matter, so trim hedges, clear gutters and pressure wash the driveway. Inside, fix leaks, stains and sticking doors. Buyers from out of state often ask about the roof and the air conditioning, so note their ages and keep the receipts.

If you plan to take a cash offer as is, you still gain by listing the problems you know about. A buyer who sees a clear list can price the repairs without padding the offer for unknowns.

faqs.q: What is the gap between foreclosure judgment and auction?
faqs.a: The clerk schedules the sale 20 to 35 days after judgment unless the lender consents to a later date (s. 45.031).

faqs.q: Can I get surplus money after a foreclosure sale?
faqs.a: Yes, if any remains after liens and the judgment. File a claim with the clerk before the funds are reported as unclaimed.

faqs.q: Does a tax certificate mean I lose my house right away?
faqs.a: No. A deed application cannot be filed until two years have run from April 1 of the issue year (s. 197.502). Ask the Broward tax collector what clearing it would cost.

faqs.q: How does the Florida tax deferral work?
faqs.a: The owner files Form DR-570 with the tax collector, deferring the part above 5 percent of last year's household income.

faqs.q: Who provides water and sewer in Margate?
faqs.a: The city provides water, wastewater and stormwater service, so a closing should include a final utility reading.
